title: Harvard Endowment Reveals $2.2 Billion SpaceX Stake, Its Largest Single Holding
excerpt: The filing shows SpaceX dwarfs Harvard's other equity positions, highlighting the enormous returns university endowments reaped from early venture capital exposure to Elon Musk's company.
body:
• Harvard Management Company disclosed a $2.2 billion stake in SpaceX in a regulatory filing, making it the endowment's largest individual stock holding by a wide margin.
  • The position represents roughly 12.9 million shares in Elon Musk's rocket and internet company, which went public in a record-setting IPO in June.
  • Harvard's SpaceX holding dwarfs its next-largest positions — approximately $350 million in Taiwan Semiconductor and $234 million in Amazon.
  • Other university endowments including the University of California, UNC, and Washington University in St. Louis also disclosed significant SpaceX positions.

Harvard University's endowment fund holds a $2.2 billion stake in SpaceX, a regulatory filing revealed Friday, exposing the scale of the university's bet on Elon Musk's rocket, satellite internet, and AI company following its blockbuster public debut in June.

Harvard Management Company, which oversees roughly $57 billion in assets, reported the position in a Form 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The roughly 12.9 million shares make SpaceX the single largest individual stock holding in Harvard's $4.3 billion portfolio of U.S. equities — more than six times its next-largest position in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, valued at approximately $350 million, and nearly ten times its $234 million Amazon stake.

The IPO Windfall

The filing underscores the enormous returns that university endowments reaped from early exposure to SpaceX, often gained through venture capital fund investments made more than a decade ago. SpaceX's June initial public offering was the largest in history, with the company debuting at $135 per share and carrying a valuation above $2.1 trillion at the closing bell.

SpaceX shares have fluctuated since the IPO, closing at $140 on Friday — up 3.7% from the offering price but well off the highs that followed the listing. The company currently carries a valuation of more than $1.8 trillion.

Harvard's position could include both shares owned directly and stock distributed to the university through private investment funds that held pre-IPO stakes.

A Broader University Windfall

Harvard is far from the only academic institution benefiting from SpaceX's transition to public markets. The University of California's investment arm disclosed a position worth roughly $1 billion in a separate filing this week. The University of North Carolina and Washington University in St. Louis also reported holdings.

"We obviously hope for every co-investment to get this large, but few businesses compound at this rate for such a long period of time."

— Scott Wilson, Chief Investment Officer, Washington University in St. Louis

Washington University's SpaceX investment has delivered more than a 3,000% return, according to Bloomberg. The endowment's CIO Scott Wilson placed roughly $50 million in SpaceX nearly a decade ago, and the position has grown to represent more than 10% of the school's $17 billion in assets.

Managing Concentration Risk

The windfall creates a new challenge: concentration risk. Endowments that traditionally diversify across asset classes now find themselves with outsized exposure to a single public company whose stock is subject to market volatility.

Some institutions have already begun trimming. Washington University sold shares on the secondary market before the IPO and plans to reduce its position further. The University of North Carolina's board has discussed whether and how to hedge its SpaceX exposure now that the company trades publicly, according to people familiar with the endowment's planning.

For large endowments, the gains arrive at a welcome moment. University finances face pressure from uncertainty over federal research funding, demographic shifts reducing the pool of college-age students, and weaker returns from traditional private equity investments. Endowment funds managing more than $500 million returned a median 18.9% before fees in the year ended in June, according to the Wilshire Trust Universe Comparison Service.

SpaceX's Expanding Empire

SpaceX has evolved well beyond its origins as a rocket-launching company. The firm now operates Starlink, one of the world's largest satellite internet providers, and has expanded into AI with plans for orbital data centers. That diversification has underpinned a valuation that would have seemed inconceivable even a few years ago.

Investment managers overseeing more than $100 million in U.S. equities are required to submit Form 13F filings within 45 days after each quarter's end, providing a snapshot of holdings in publicly traded securities. The filings do not specify when positions were acquired.
